chunks: And in the causes mentioned by al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān, may Allah have mercy on him, from al-Riḍā عليه السلام, he said:

The salat for the eclipse was only instituted because it is among the signs of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and it is not known whether it has appeared as a mercy or as a punishment. So the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم loved that his community should turn in alarm to its Creator and its Merciful One at that time, so that He may avert from them its evil and protect them from its harm, just as He turned it away from the people of Yūnus عليه السلام when they implored Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
And it was only made ten rakʿahs because the original salat whose obligation was first sent down from the heaven in the day and the night was only ten rakʿahs, so those rakʿahs were gathered here.

And prostration was only placed in it because there is no salat in which there is bowing except that there is also prostration in it, and so that they may also conclude their salat with prostration and humility.

And it was only made four sajdahs because every salat whose prostration falls short of four sajdahs is not a salat, since the least obligatory amount of prostration in salat cannot be less than four sajdahs.

And prostration was not made in place of bowing because salat while standing is more excellent than salat while sitting, and because the one standing sees the eclipse and what is above, while the one prostrating does not see.

And it was only changed from the original salat that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made obligatory because it is performed for the cause of a change in one of the matters, namely the eclipse. So when the cause changed, the effect changed.

key_terms.آيَاتِ اللَّهِ: the signs of Allah, indicating a divine sign that calls for reflection and response
key_terms.الرُّكُوعِ: bowing, the repeated act around which the eclipse prayer is structured
key_terms.السُّجُودُ: prostration, an essential element included in the prayer along with bowing
key_terms.الْعِلَّةُ: the effective cause or reason for a ruling
key_terms.الْكُسُوفِ: the eclipse, the event for which this special salat is legislated
key_terms.الْمَعْلُولُ: the resultant ruling or effect that follows from the cause
key_terms.صَلَاةٌ: salat, the prescribed ritual prayer discussed here in its eclipse form
key_terms.عَشْرَ رَكَعَاتٍ: ten rakʿahs, the total number assigned to this prayer in the hadith

ai.seo_question: Why was the eclipse prayer legislated, and why does it differ from the regular form of salat?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the reason for salat al-kusuf, presenting the eclipse as one of the signs of Allah, the meaning of which may be mercy or warning, and therefore a moment for the Ummah to turn to Allah in humility. It also gives a juridical rationale for the structure of the prayer, including its ten rakʿahs, its sajdahs, and its distinct form, based on the principle that when the cause changes, the associated ruling also changes.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1510 - In the explanations attributed to al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, narrated from Imam al-Ridha (as), He said:

"The prayer for the eclipse was instituted because it is one of the signs of Allah (swt), Blessed and Exalted, and it is not known whether it appeared as a mercy or as a punishment. Therefore, The Prophet (sw) wanted his community to turn in supplication to their Creator and Merciful Lord (azj) at such moments so that He might avert its harm from them and protect them from its displeasure, just as He protected the people of Yunus (Jonah) when they turned to Allah (swt), the Mighty and Glorious, in supplication."

He continued: "It was established with ten units of prayer because the original prayer, whose obligation was revealed from the heavens, initially consisted of ten units during the day and night, so these units were combined here.
The inclusion of prostration is because any prayer that contains bowing must also contain prostration, and it serves to conclude their prayer with submission and humility.
Four prostrations were specified because any prayer lacking four prostrations cannot be considered a valid prayer, as the minimum obligatory prostrations in a prayer are four.

The reason that bowing (Ruku') was not substituted with prostration is that prayer standing up is superior to prayer sitting down, and because one standing can witness the eclipse above, whereas one in prostration cannot see it."

He added: "The prayer for the eclipse was altered from the original form of prayer that Allah (swt), the Mighty and Glorious, had prescribed because it is performed due to a change in one of the natural phenomena, the eclipse. When the cause changes, the practice associated with it changes accordingly."
